Neutral fraction is absent in both molecules, so it does not alter the comparison. Even with chloroalkene and QED working against it, Neighbor 5 still ends up reinforcing the non-mutagenic label because the query is substantially larger and more polar.

Neighbor 6 is the strongest of the negative neighbors in terms of exposure-related counterweights. Neutral fraction remains absent in both molecules, so there is no differentiating ionization effect there. The carboxylic acid count is unchanged at 2, so that feature does not help separate the pair. Taken together, Neighbor 6 is still dominated by the query’s larger, less permeable character, which outweighs the chloroalkene and QED signals and supports the non-mutagenic class.

Taken together, the local analog evidence supports option (A): is not mutagenic.
